US_force.surface_cover: Most fast battleships/cruisers remain with carrier screen because Japanese resistance and submarine warning make a historical leaker-hunt detachment lower-value unless a major surface target appears.

first_sweep_and_immediate_suppression.effect: Runways/revetments and one or more peripheral radar/communications/fire-direction elements are hit, but dispersal, backup power and component separation prevent immediate system decapitation.

US_daylight_operational_choice.logic: Because lagoon shipping density is lower and Japanese air-defense/repair system remains coherent, more sorties than in a historical-style shipping massacre are assigned to deliberate base-system suppression.
priority: warning radar/plot/communications and AA fire-direction components
US_daylight_operational_choice.constraint: Kwajalein-captured evidence improves U.S. awareness that antenna/power/plot/communications are separable targets, but 10 days is insufficient for complete technical exploitation of Japanese passive-warning equipment.

day1_air_exchange_cumulative.interpretation: US obtains practical daylight air superiority at materially higher cost than historical HAILSTONE; prepared Japanese defense avoids a first-hour massacre but cannot match repeated U.S. deck cycles.

fixed_base_damage_by_dusk.airfields: All major strips cratered/cycle-limited; at least one strip can still support emergency/small-package launches after repair-party work.
fixed_base_damage_by_dusk.precision_AA_channels: one reliable centered; a second intermittent/local
fixed_base_damage_by_dusk.communications_power: local outages; low-bandwidth command connectivity survives through redundancy and alternate power.

shipping_and_escape.last_convoy: one western picket obtains a night/periscope-radar contact; center result is one medium 4,000-7,000 GRT merchant/auxiliary sunk or constructive total loss; a second hit is sensitivity only.

lagoon_day1_losses.destroyer: 0 sunk centered; 1 destroyer/escort mission-limited or damaged centered

shipping_and_escape.guard: No carrier, Akashi, fleet oiler, Katori-class force or other high-value historical leaker is inserted merely to recreate historical surface combat.

surface_and_submarine.US_surface_sweep: No full historical Iowa/New Jersey leaker-hunt centered. Fast battleships stay with carrier screen unless a valuable escape group is actually found.
surface_and_submarine.Japan_submarine_result: one coarse carrier-screen sector contact possible; no satisfactory daylight torpedo shot centered; one boat mission-damaged/forced outward centered.
surface_and_submarine.Japan_surface_fleet_counter_sortie: NO-GO; major fleet units continue westward preservation.

night_counterstrike_gate.cue: 1-3 hour old submarine/RI/DF/water-air sector picture, not exact carrier fix
night_counterstrike_gate.US_state: high alert after costly daylight defense; fast battleships remain concentrated with TF58.
